observation.visible_scene: A transparent cylindrical container filled with water, set against a pure black background, with a splash crown in mid-evolution. The crown consists of two tall lateral spikes (left and right), each capped by a droplet, connected by a thin curved wall, plus a turbulent vertical column of water rising from the center. Numerous small free droplets are suspended in the air above the crown. The excerpt captures this structure deforming over time; the splash is already fully formed at the first frame and is still changing at the last.
visible_changes: Relative to the container rim, both lateral crown spikes shorten and tilt outward; the droplets at their tips descend and move farther apart (left tip drifts down-left, right tip down-right).
The crown wall joining the spikes subsides: its upper edge lowers and becomes more ragged and broken as the excerpt progresses.
The central vertical column persists throughout; a rounded blob/droplet forms and grows at its apex, while the mound of water at the column's base rises and sprouts small peripheral spikes.
Free airborne droplets above the crown drift upward and outward, spreading across the top of the frame; some new small droplets appear among them.
The water surface inside the container shows evolving ripples and a deforming meniscus near the rim.
The whole container-and-crown assembly shifts slightly downward within the frame over time, with horizontal position essentially unchanged.
outside_clip_unknowns: What object or impact produced the crown (the motion is already underway at t=0).
Whether the crown ultimately collapses back into the container and whether the surface settles after t=2.667.
uncertain_details: Whether the downward drift of the scene is a slow camera tilt/pan or actual settling of the container/water (no background reference to disambiguate).
The exact moment, if any, at which the rounded droplet atop the central column detaches versus merely oscillating.
